summary.intent: Plan and then execute Phase 69 of CipherBox (a privacy-first encrypted cloud storage system): port the node/v3 model to the Rust desktop stack (FUSE/WinFsp), making clients grant-root-aware and mirroring the TS Phase 68.2 SDK-owned read chain, then continue straight into execution per user authorization.
summary.outcome: Planning ballooned from 14 to 25 plans across three rounds of in-execution architectural discovery (missing write-plane infra, missing write-owner materialization, missing legacy-type retirement, missing desktop root-key recovery); 22 of 25 plans were merged with the workspace kept green throughout, including a successful 11-slice atomic FUSE cutover that had blocked three times. Session ended mid-grind on the final root-key-recovery plans (69-23 launching) with WinFsp (69-14) still deferred to the user's Windows machine and desktop-e2e still unrun, per the user's explicit requirement that real root-key recovery must be wired before the phase can be called complete.

repo: GSD's commit helper frequently reports 'commit_failed' even when the commit actually lands (lint-staged completes but the wrapper misreports) — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

Worktree executors sometimes mis-report `expected_base` in `<worktree_metadata>` as their own last docs commit rather than the true fork point — verify via `git merge-base <branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.

Running `cargo fmt` from a crate root (e.g. lib.rs) recursively reformats the whole module tree; executors must `git checkout --` any out-of-scope reformatted files before committing to keep diffs scoped.

Legacy folder-model types (FolderMetadata/FilePointer/FolderEntry/FileMetadata) were still load-bearing for the recycle-bin, vault-export, and vault-creation subsystems — a 'delete all legacy types' plan (D-04/69-10) written before those subsystems were migrated cannot run as written.

The desktop app was still on the legacy v2 single-key vault blob while the web app had already shipped vault-blob-v3 (two independent random root keys, ECIES-wrapped) in PR #578 — meaning a web-created vault was literally unreadable by the desktop client until this gap was found and ported.

`gsd-planner` can crash mid-run on an API error after writing most plans to disk; recovery is to spawn a fresh single-plan planner for just the missing plan rather than restart the whole planning pass.

Background worktree executors can die on account/session usage limits (not architectural issues) — distinguish by checking whether the worktree has any commits/edits before treating it as a real blocker.
The desktop E2E CI workflow's real name is 'Desktop E2E Tests', not 'CI E2E Tests' as an earlier ROADMAP/CONTEXT doc worded it — using the wrong name in `gh workflow run` would 404.

code.finding: JournalOp never had a `parent_metadata: FolderMetadata` field as research claimed — that field actually lived in fuse-side `MkdirJournalResult`; a re-scope plan built around this 'cross-crate weld' had to be corrected before execution.

InodeKind is a full read-write vault-owner state (stores folder_key/ipns_private_key/file_ipns_private_key) — the FUSE mount signs IPNS records and seals children, unlike the read-only web 68.2 client, so a read-only gated listing API alone cannot drive the flip.

resolve_child unseals a child's read key and immediately zeroizes it; ResolvedChild carries no key material at all, which is why a separate write-owner materialization API (list_folder_owned/ResolvedOwnedChild) had to be built for the FUSE mount.

Desktop derived node/v3 root read/write keys via a placeholder bridge (`root_write_key = root_read_key ^ 0xA5`) from the legacy `root_folder_key`, since real node/v3 root-key recovery into KeyState was never wired — this bridge had to be replaced by a genuine vault-blob-v3 port.

New vault-blob-v3 codec added: `0x03 | u16_BE(readLen) | ECIES(rootReadKey) | u16_BE(writeLen) | ECIES(rootWriteKey)`, byte-matched against the frozen cross-language KAT `tests/vectors/vault-v3-blob.json`; v2 codec left untouched for compatibility.

workflow: For a genuinely atomic, all-or-nothing multi-thousand-line cutover, chunk it into bounded 'slices' executed sequentially on the same worktree branch, each committing independently (RED-elsewhere is fine), with a committed runbook recording the frozen target shape and each slice's carry-forward facts — this survives session/usage-limit interruptions without losing coherence.

When a subagent reports an architectural blocker with concrete grep/line evidence, independently re-verify the specific claims against the live tree before accepting or escalating to the user — this caught that some 'evidence' was accurate while catching one instance of an agent's own mis-capture (expected_base).

For crypto/security-critical code, prefer gating final correctness on a live end-to-end test run over trusting `cargo check`/unit-test green alone — compile-green and mock-tested crypto has shipped runtime-broken before in this project.

When an unattended agent hits a scope/architecture wall it can't safely resolve, having it make zero edits and report findings (rather than force partial/unverifiable work) preserves a clean, mergeable baseline for the orchestrator to re-plan from.

friction: Three separate architectural blockers were discovered only during execution, not during planning/research, each requiring a stop-the-line re-scope (research + planner + user decision) before execution could resume — this repeatedly derailed the 'plan once, execute straight through' assumption.
Long-running opus executor agents twice died mid-task on account/session usage limits (unrelated to task difficulty), requiring detection, waiting for reset, and re-dispatch.
The gsd commit-helper false-negative ('commit_failed' when the commit actually succeeded) recurred on essentially every commit, requiring manual git log verification each time.
One executor mis-reported its own worktree's fork base in `<worktree_metadata>`, which could have caused a bad merge if not independently verified.
Working directory (cwd) drifted at least twice mid-session, causing a scratchpad write to go to a malformed doubled path and a commit attempt to fail, both requiring correction to absolute paths.

Scope grew substantially and repeatedly (14→16→18→20→25 plans) as each 'final' blocker uncovered a deeper missing subsystem, extending the session across multiple usage-limit resets and a manual pause/resume.
open_items: Plans 69-23, 69-24, 69-25 (desktop vault init/recovery to v3, mount wiring deleting the ^0xA5 bridge, and the e2e verifier fix) still need to be executed and merged.
A real local desktop-e2e run (Postgres/api/Kubo/Redis/mock-ipns-routing + FUSE-T stack) still needs to be executed as the user-mandated completion gate, once root-key recovery lands.
69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration, TEST-03/SC#5) remains `autonomous:false` and deferred to the user's own Windows machine.

ROT-07: no production `RotationDeps` implementor exists yet, so shared-scope-exit deletes/renames on Unix currently fail closed (EIO) until live wiring is done — documented as a known limitation, not fixed in this phase.
No live Rust bin-restore (recycle-bin undelete) command exists yet — 69-19 only landed the restore *data* shape plus a round-trip proof, not an actual restore command.
Phase 69 branch (`feat/fuse-and-winfsp-rust-integration-and-grant-root-awareness`) is not yet pushed and no PR has been opened.
